vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 29. Nay or No: 10. Not Voting: 1. stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text:
I’ll be joining Lori Townsend on tomorrow’s Talk of Alaska at 10:00 a.m.! Be sure to call in with your questions: 907-550-8422 in Anchorage or 1-800-478-8255 statewide.

Looking forward to hearing from you! https://t.co/CeYwJadbYH
Great news for Alaska and the nation! https://t.co/jvXyKZTu0E
To our veterans, thank you for all you have done and continue to do. Our country is forever indebted to you for your service and sacrifice. https://t.co/Xr6uA3A0Fd

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act—BAAJA—will meaningfully reform the broken federal permitting process. That has been a priority of mine for many years, and I credit my colleagues @SenMikeLee, @SenatorHeinrich, @SenCapito, and @SenWhitehouse for their good work on a complex subject.

While I voted to advance BAAJA, I have heard and share the concerns that many Tribes and Tribal Organizations have raised about changes being made to the National Historic Preservation Act. We have worked for weeks with the bill’s sponsors to make meaningful progress on many of those issues through their substitute amendment, but we can and should do more.

As we begin floor debate, I look forward to more work with my colleagues as we seek to make this bill even better.

Alaskans don’t need any help voting for their preferred candidates, and the State of Alaska has already handled this by clearly distinguishing the candidates on this year’s ballot. The Department of Justice should never have filed this lawsuit.

https://t.co/88tGvV0P8O

In 1966, Alaska Native leaders came together from different regions, speaking different languages and facing different challenges. But they united around the lands and traditions that had sustained their people for countless generations.

Six decades later, we gathered at the https://t.co/NiXce1pl4m

I’m relieved that the Homeland Security Department has maintained Temporary Protected Status for Ukrainians who have sought refuge in the United States, including many who now call Alaska home. But with no end in sight to Russia’s brutal war, I urge the administration to act

On #IndigenousPeoplesDay, we celebrate the cultures of Alaska Native peoples. For countless generations, Alaska Native communities have carried forward their languages, knowledge, and traditions, helping shape the state we are proud to call home.

One year ago, Typhoon Halong changed lives forever in Western Alaska. I will never forget seeing the devastation firsthand. Unfortunately, for families in Kipnuk and Kwigillingok, recovery continues, and many are still displaced and uncertain about what comes next.

I’m grateful to the Tribal leaders, first responders, volunteers, and community members who have stepped up to help others through this extraordinarily difficult time. It makes me proud to see Alaskans supporting Alaskans, but that resilience must also be met with meaningful federal support. I will continue working to improve disaster preparedness and recovery for communities across our state.

One year later, we cannot look away. I remain committed to standing with affected communities, listening to their voices, and ensuring they have the opportunity to shape their path toward healing and long-term recovery.

A few weeks ago, Congress overwhelmingly passed legislation to increase sanctions and tariffs on Russia. The President should be using those authorities instead of allowing Russia to export diesel, rake in revenues, and continue its catastrophic war in Ukraine. We can discuss Russia’s return to global energy markets once the war is over, but in the meantime, we need to cut off everything fueling it.

https://t.co/KPkEoDy1Np

There is no need to livestream any execution, including this one. I would expect this from terrorists and dictators, but not here in America. It would give this individual, who deserves no further notoriety, the martyrdom he seeks. How we carry out justice matters just as much as the justice itself, so I urge the Pentagon to reverse this gruesome decision.

https://t.co/HtKIy8FpBX

Senator Stevens was a tireless champion for Alaska and the men and women who serve our nation, and it was an honor to celebrate his name joining one of the most formidable warships of the 21st century. I know Captain Hays and her crew will proudly carry on Uncle Ted’s legacy of commitment and service. Fair winds and following seas, and lead with courage! ⚓️
Congrats to Backpack on becoming the 2026 Fat Bear Week Champion and showing the world how Alaskans get through the winter: eating a lot of salmon! https://t.co/1FsxytsNzh

This unprecedented announcement moves our long-sought Alaska natural gas pipeline closer than ever to construction and operation. South Korea’s commitment to invest $54 billion to build the gasline will deliver significant benefits for Alaskans, from good jobs to affordable energy. 

I look forward to learning more about the timing of South Korea’s investments and other key details of this agreement, and I thank President Trump and his administration, Senator Sullivan—who has led the way on this project—Congressman Begich, and Governor Dunleavy. This has been a team effort, and we need to keep going until the gas is flowing.

https://t.co/ecwKlyMfB8
On Orange Shirt Day, the National Day of Remembrance for Indian Boarding School Survivors, we honor the children who returned home and remember those who never did. 🧡 https://t.co/uwLMreGWAE

For those living with ALS, every day matters. 

They cannot afford disruptions in research, treatment access, and support. This reauthorization ensures that the momentum we have built over the past five years will continue, keeping pathways to promising investigational treatments open while supporting the research needed to find better treatments and, ultimately, a cure. 

I’m grateful to Senator Coons, Representatives Quigley and Calvert, and especially the ALS community, whose persistence helped us get this legislation across the finish line before the authorization expired.

President Trump has made recent statements about the Kennedy Center and the ‘Triumphal Arch,’ giving very little context or content about either to Congress or the public.

Any action to demolish facilities authorized by Congress or to construct facilities on federal land first requires rigorous oversight and explicit congressional approval. I would ask the Trump administration to work with us and present actual plans, including cost estimates, for these projects rather than circumventing their responsibility to American taxpayers.

https://t.co/lHSlRbN9Nv

I have spent time with many Ukrainians who have found a home in Alaska after fleeing Russia’s brutal invasion. They have become part of our communities, sending their children to our schools, participating in the local workforce, and rebuilding their lives while the war continues to devastate their home country.

My office has worked with many of these families as they navigate our immigration system, and the reality is that it is simply not safe for them to return to Ukraine. We should not force Ukrainians—whom we allowed into the U.S. and who are here legally and contributing to our communities—back into an active war zone.

These two pieces of legislation will provide them with the stability and protection they need to continue to live and work here until it is safe to return to their home.

https://t.co/gorGowvga8

Permitting reform is one of the best things we can do for our country, and the package negotiated in the Senate is objectively good for our country. We should take it up and pass it this work period, instead of waiting and potentially missing our window.

The racial and rural disparities in maternal and infant mortality rates in this country are alarming and unacceptable.

Our legislation works to address this by investing in innovative approaches to maternal health care, improving data collection, strengthening support for women during the postpartum period, and expanding the use of telehealth in rural communities. 

Whether you’re in Napakiak or New York City, every mother and child deserves access to quality care, and the programs implemented through this bill will help bring us closer to that goal.

https://t.co/4lQGyKEC3u

Yom Kippur is a time of reflection, repentance, and forgiveness, and one of the most sacred days in Judaism. I wish all those observing a peaceful and contemplative fast. G’mar Chatima Tova. https://t.co/c7nP10cGAx

I’m encouraged that our nations have reached a breakthrough that respects Greenlandic self-determination and the sovereignty of the Kingdom of Denmark while strengthening our shared security in the Arctic.

I’m hopeful that this agreement will build upon the longstanding framework established by the 1951 Defense of Greenland Agreement, adapting our cooperation to address today’s security challenges while preserving the foundation that has supported our partnership. I have always had faith in the enduring friendship between the United States, Greenland, and Denmark, and I believe this agreement represents an important opportunity to further strengthen our bond.

https://t.co/rv96SPIV0L

The Office of Management and Budget has proposed revisions that could significantly change how federal grants and financial assistance are administered, including funding that supports Tribal governments and organizations across Alaska and the nation. 

I sent a letter to OMB urging meaningful government-to-government consultation and calling for any final rule to recognize the unique political and legal status of Tribes, uphold the federal trust, treaty and statutory obligations, and fully account for the impacts on Tribal governments and the essential services they provide. For Tribes, changes to federal grant administration could affect resources for health care, housing, education, public safety, infrastructure, child welfare, and more.

https://t.co/dHSqcPAdtk

Alaska has the highest suicide rate in the United States, at more than double the national average. In 2025, more young people in Alaska died by suicide than in any other year in the past decade.

I appreciated the chance to engage with Dr. Westlake, nominee to be HHS Assistant Secretary for Mental Health and Substance Use, about how we can improve Alaska’s mental health outcomes. It must start with addressing our severe shortage of mental health professionals, and I will work with Dr. Westlake to increase access to providers across our state.

For too long, federal programs have been developed forNative communities instead of with them, resulting in fragmented systems that react to crises instead of preventing them. Tribes know their children, their communities and what works. When given the authority, flexibility and resources to lead, tribes create solutions grounded in culture, family, community and accountability.

Ultimately, this legislation is not about reports or bureaucracy. It is about whether a child in a remote village can access mental health care without leaving home. It is about whether parents can keep their family together during hardship. It is about whether Native youth can grow up with opportunity grounded in culture, language, community and hope.

Most of all, it is about the voices that started this conversation.
https://t.co/4Ic7mFltII

This morning, I am attending a memorial ceremony at Fort Wainwright as we mark the 25th anniversary of the deadliest terrorist attacks in our nation’s history. 

The attacks of September 11, 2001, claimed the lives of nearly 3,000 Americans, including hundreds of first responders who charged into the destruction to rescue others. We remember all who were lost, from the innocents trapped on hijacked planes and in burning buildings to the heroes who perished saving their fellow citizens. 

We also honor our nation’s military men and women, who answered the call to serve. Thousands of soldiers deployed from Alaska and fought courageously in Afghanistan, Iraq, and beyond. Many came home wounded and some never came home at all, sacrificing everything on our behalf.   

While we have lost much of the national unity that prevailed a quarter-century ago, we have prevented similar attacks on our soil. We know who to thank for that: our military, our law enforcement, and our first responders. 

On this September 11, we remember the fallen and honor the patriots whose bravery continues to keep us safe.

For decades, Alaska Native leaders and ANTHC have led the charge to bring the Alaska Native Medical Center into Tribal ownership. I’ve been proud to support that vision through my work in the Senate by securing vital resources, advancing land transfers, promoting self-determination, and holding the federal government accountable to its commitments to Alaska Native people.

This transfer will create new opportunities for investment and improvements at ANMC, strengthening the Tribal health system and, in turn, health care across Alaska. I’m honored to have been a partner in this effort, and I will continue working to ensure Alaska Native communities have the resources, authority, and opportunity to shape their own health care future.

https://t.co/AGdOq5kk5V

I join Alaskans in grieving the loss of the four people who perished in the plane crash in Seldovia yesterday. This month has been a painful reminder of the realities of travel in Alaska. Our vast distances and lack of road connections mean we depend on aviation to knit our state together, which makes accidents like this all the more heartbreaking. I’m grateful to the Alaska State Troopers and all who responded to the scene, and I’m praying for their families, loved ones, and the Seldovia community as they mourn this terrible loss.

https://t.co/2MSoLcJM4z

I join Alaskans in condolences as we learn of the plane crash in Cape Newenham today. I’ve traveled extensively with Security Aviation throughout Alaska, and have met many of their experienced pilots. I appreciate the U.S. Coast Guard, NTSB, Alaska State Troopers, and the Rescue Coordination Center for responding to the site. Alaska is praying for those on board, their loved ones, and the team at Security Aviation. 

https://t.co/QZNtUvUbtH

I am pleased that Kyle Reardon has been nominated to serve as a United States District Judge for the District of Alaska. Kyle brings extensive knowledge of both our state and our court system to the federal bench, having served the District of Alaska as a federal prosecutor and U.S. Magistrate Judge, a position he has held in Alaska for the past five years. His extensive experience, professionalism, and judicial temperament make him exceptionally well-qualified for this role. I thank the President for nominating Kyle and helping bring Alaska’s District Court back to full capacity.

https://t.co/MDzZMiB1Sh

The other week, I raised this issue with Secretary McMahon, and I’m pleased she agreed to expedite the obligation of the funds for the Alaska Native Education Program grants that Congress appropriated earlier this year.

ANEP helps Alaska Native Tribes, Tribal organizations, eligible schools, and other organizations meet the needs of Alaska Native students in wide variety of ways. Grants provide, for example, culturally relevant curriculum, tutoring and other academic supports, indigenous language revitalization, workforce development opportunities, teacher professional development, postsecondary planning and support, and success, early childhood education, and afterschool programming. 

I will continue to champion this program and work with the Department to ensure this funding is administered more expeditiously going forward.

https://t.co/qF8PUrFPs9

Without accurate stock assessments, we cannot make the informed, science-based management decisions needed to ensure our fisheries remain sustainable for generations to come. Environmental DNA is an innovative, cost-effective tool that will give our scientists a clearer picture of our fisheries while expanding survey coverage and reducing costs. 

This legislation is the product of extensive collaboration with NOAA, Alaska fishermen, Tribal partners, academia, and industry to modernize how we assess fish stocks using the best available science.

https://t.co/mTcxNECaKt

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
